questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Czech Republic?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Czech Republic article.

questions.proof: The capital and biggest city is Prague.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Czech Republic?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Czech Republic on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Czech Republic article.

questions.proof: Czechia has no sea; its neighbour countries are Germany, Austria, Slovakia, and Poland.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The others are Šumava National Park, Podyjí National Park, Bohemian _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Bohemian”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Czech Republic article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: The others are Šumava National Park, Podyjí National Park, Bohemian Switzerland.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The area of the today's Czechia was a part of Czechoslovakia (current area of Czechia and Slovak republic) from _____ to 1992.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Czech Republic article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: The area of the today's Czechia was a part of Czechoslovakia (current area of Czechia and Slovak republic) from 1918 to 1992.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Czechoslovakia peacefully split into two countries (Czechia and Slovakia) in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Czech Republic article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Czechoslovakia peacefully split into two countries (Czechia and Slovakia) in 1993.
